explanations.answer: They will endure reproach of their own
explanations.explanation: That's it. God says, "I have sworn with an uplifted hand that surely the nations around you will endure reproach of their own." The mountains endured reproach, and now the nations will too. And He swore it with an uplifted hand.

explanations.answer: They will rule over the mountains forever
explanations.explanation: That's the very thing God is turning around. The nations had made the mountains desolate, and God says He has sworn that they "will endure reproach of their own." Nobody is ruling forever in this verse. The oath goes the other direction.

explanations.answer: They will be left completely untouched

explanations.answer: It will be tilled and sown
explanations.explanation: That's it. God says, "I am on your side; I will turn toward you, and you will be tilled and sown." Tilled means someone's working the ground again, and sown means seed is going in. Nobody sows a field they've given up on.

explanations.answer: It will be fenced and guarded
explanations.explanation: I can see the thinking, but God doesn't mention fences or guards. He says that when He turns toward the mountains, "you will be tilled and sown." The promise is about the ground being worked and planted. I'd call that more hopeful than a fence.

explanations.answer: It will be left to rest
explanations.explanation: Resting is a nice idea, but that's not what God says. He says, "I will turn toward you, and you will be tilled and sown." The land goes back to work, and that's the good news.

explanations.answer: To make them prosper more than before
explanations.explanation: That's right. God says, "I will make you as inhabited as you once were, and I will make you prosper more than before." Back to how it was, and then more. I think that's God being generous, and I'm leaning in again.

explanations.answer: To let them prosper for a season
explanations.explanation: A season is a nice length of time, but God doesn't put a time on it. He says, "I will make you prosper more than before." The promise is bigger than before, not shorter. No season is mentioned.

explanations.answer: To keep them small and quiet
explanations.explanation: That's not in the verse at all. God says He'll make the mountains as inhabited as they once were, and "I will make you prosper more than before." More, not less. Small and quiet isn't the plan.
